speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To help narrow down the cause, on which specific side of your neck and arm are these symptoms located?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (or severe Cervical Radiculopathy) with progressive neurological deficit.

The patient's 58-year-old male with diabetes and hypertension reports a year-long history of burning neck/arm pain and paresthesias, now worsening with increasing bilateral hand weakness. Given the progressive motor deficit, I need to confirm the level of compression.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine.
REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical MRI.
